items.title: Stock Radar: Breakout from bullish pennant pattern makes Deepak Nitrite an attractive buy
items.description: Deepak Nitrite Ltd has broken out from a bullish pennant pattern on daily charts, signaling potential for further upside. Experts suggest short-term traders can target Rs 1,900 in the next 2-3 weeks, with a stop loss below Rs 1,760. The stock has shown strong recent performance and a bullish technical setup.

items.title: SBI shares in focus ahead of Q4 results; lender set to consider up to $2 billion fundraising plan on May 12
items.description: State Bank of India's board will consider a fundraising plan of up to $2 billion on May 12. The bank will also release its Q4 results today, with analysts expecting muted profit growth due to treasury losses, despite stable loan growth and margins. SBI shares have seen significant gains over the past year.

items.title: Polycab India among 3 stocks flashing bullish signals, hinting at a possible uptrend
items.description: On May 7, three stocks from the Nifty 200 segment appeared on the White Marubozu bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern that forms when the opening price is the lowest, and the closing price is the highest for the session.It is represented by a long bullish candlestick with little to no shadows, indicating strong buying pressure throughout the session. Traders interpret it as a sign that buyers dominated from open to close, often using it to identify potential continuation of upward price trends.

items.title: KPIT Technologies among 5 F&O stocks with a sharp rise in futures open interest
items.description: As of May 07, five stocks in the NSE F&O pack saw a notable surge in futures open interest, contributing to a total increase in open interest of over 10% compared with the previous trading session. A significant uptick in futures open interest signifies substantial growth in the number of active, unexpired futures contracts in a specific security. This uptrend reflects an increasing number of participants either initiating new positions or expanding the size of their existing positions in the futures market.

items.title: Pidilite Industries shares in focus after Q4 net profit jumps 37% to Rs 584 crore, revenue rises 14%
items.description: Pidilite Industries reported a 36.6% year-on-year jump in Q4FY26 net profit to Rs 584.2 crore, with revenue rising 14.1%. Margin expansion was driven by lower input costs. The company also posted steady full-year growth, supported by strong performance in its Consumer and Bazaar segment and stable demand conditions.

items.title: Dabur shares in focus as Q4 net profit rises 15% to Rs 369 crore, revenue up 7.3%
items.description: Dabur India reported a 15% year-on-year rise in Q4FY26 net profit to Rs 369 crore, with revenue increasing 7.3%. Growth was driven by strong domestic FMCG performance and volume expansion. However, profits declined sequentially. The company also saw broad-based category growth and modest international business expansion.

items.title: Hero MotoCorp among 7 stocks showing bullish RSI upswing
items.description: Seven stocks from the Nifty500 segment were identified in the RSI Trending Up scan on May 7, based on data from StockEdge.com. An uptrend signal is generated when the RSI value crosses above 50 from below. “RSI trending up” indicates strengthening price momentum, which may signal potential upward movement and help traders spot buying opportunities.

items.title: OnEMI Technology shares to list today. GMP signals at one of the strongest debuts in recent past
items.description: OnEMI Technology Solutions, the company behind Kissht, is poised for its stock market debut. Grey market trends suggest a strong listing, with shares expected to trade above the issue price. The IPO saw significant demand, particularly from institutional investors. Proceeds will bolster the company's NBFC subsidiary for future loan growth. Investors anticipate a successful debut for this fintech player.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 8 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, 16 stocks closed above their 200-day moving average (DMA) on May 7, 2026, according to technical scan data from StockEdge. Among these, we have highlighted the top eight stocks that posted gains of more than 3%. The 200-day daily moving average (DMA) is used by traders as a key indicator for determining the overall trend in a particular stock. As long as the stock is priced above the 200-day SMA on the daily timeframe, it is generally considered to be in an overall uptrend. Take a look:

items.title: Trendline Breakout Points to Bullish Reversal in Deepak Nitrite
items.description: “Deepak Nitrite stock had witnessed a phase of consolidation after which it has recently given a breakout surpassing its previous hurdle of 1780 levels. Traders can buy for a target of Rs 1900 in the next 2-3 weeks,” Shivangi Sarda, Analyst, Derivatives and Technical Research, Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd, said.

items.title: Dalal Street likely to open in red amid weak GIFT Nifty cues
items.description: Indian stock markets saw a mixed trading day on May 7. The Sensex experienced volatility due to its weekly expiry. Analysts suggest a breakout above 24,400 could lead to further gains. India VIX, a measure of market fear, declined significantly. Foreign and domestic investors were net buyers of shares.

items.title: Stocks in news: SBI, Titan, Hyundai, BSE, Torrent Pharma, Axis Bank
items.description: Indian markets saw volatile trading on Thursday, closing nearly unchanged despite positive signals. Several companies including SBI, Titan, and Hyundai are in focus today. Many firms will announce their fourth-quarter results. Britannia Industries reported strong profit growth and recommended a dividend. BSE also posted a significant profit surge. Bharat Forge's profit declined, while Dabur India saw a profit uptick.

items.title: Midcap rally hits record high amid retail buying surge
items.description: Nifty midcap indices reached new peaks on Thursday. This surge is fueled by robust earnings, consistent retail investor contributions, and strategic bargain purchases. Midcap and smallcap indices have significantly outperformed larger indices since the US-Iran ceasefire announcement a month ago. Experts suggest a pause in the rally is likely soon. Foreign investors have been selling large-cap stocks.

items.title: Foreign investors continue to pull out of financials in second half of April
items.description: Foreign investors continued their sell-off in Indian equities, particularly in financials, extending withdrawals into the latter half of April. This sector saw significant outflows due to its heavy weight and inflation concerns. Conversely, power and capital goods attracted substantial inflows, driven by strong demand and global trends.

items.title: Retail stake cut in 284 BSE 500 companies in Q4
items.description: Retail investors showed caution, reducing their stock holdings in most companies during the March quarter. This move coincided with market declines due to global uncertainties. Meanwhile, foreign investors and domestic funds increased their stakes in various companies. Promoters also raised their shareholding, taking advantage of lower stock prices. FPI stake in Indian companies continued to fall.

items.title: Foreign remittances to Kerala stay resilient despite West Asia crisis
items.description: Money from non-resident Indians to Kerala remains strong. Banks like Federal Bank and South Indian Bank show growth in deposits. This inflow is vital for Kerala's economy. A weaker rupee also boosts remittances. Experts believe inflows will continue unless job losses in the Middle East occur. A prolonged conflict could pose a long-term risk.

items.title: No AI, poor returns drive Dalal Street investors to foreign markets
items.description: Indian investors are increasingly shifting money overseas in search of diversification amid weaker domestic market returns, persistent foreign fund outflows, and a record-low rupee. Overseas investments in equities and debt rose 60% year-on-year to over $2.2 billion in the 11 months through February.

items.title: Shell’s Profit Surge: How Iran Tensions Powered Q1 Earnings
items.description: Shell reported adjusted earnings of $6.9 billion in the first quarter of 2026, comfortably beating analyst expectations. The performance marked the company’s strongest quarterly profit in nearly two years and represented a sharp rebound from the previous quarter. Strong gains from refining and energy trading operations played a major role in driving earnings higher. (Source: Barron’s, NYT, Financial Times)

items.title: BSE share price target rises up to Rs 4,570 after Q4 results. What Jefferies, Motilal Oswal & others are saying?
items.description: BSE shares dipped despite a strong March quarter performance, with net profit soaring 61% YoY to Rs 797 crore and revenue jumping 85% to Rs 1,564 crore. Analysts remain divided, with Nuvama maintaining a 'Buy' rating and Jefferies a 'Hold', citing varying growth prospects and risks.

items.title: Sonata Software shares rally 10% as Q4 net profit rises 21% despite revenue contraction; firm announces dividend
items.description: Sonata Software shares surged nearly 10% after the company reported a 21% rise in Q4 FY26 net profit, despite a decline in revenue. Strong EBITDA growth and deal wins supported sentiment, while the firm announced a final dividend. Segment performance remained steady, with gains in both international and domestic businesses.

items.title: Thermax shares jump 8% as Q4 profit rises 19% YoY to Rs 244 crore; order book strengthens
items.description: Thermax shares experienced a significant jump, reaching a new 52-week high. This surge followed the company's strong Q4FY26 financial results. Robust revenue growth and a substantial increase in order inflows were key drivers. Investors also reacted positively to attractive dividend recommendations, including a special payout for the company's 60th anniversary. The company's order book shows strong future visibility.

items.title: Sensex options can be as large as Nifty's by FY29, says Jefferies but has a warning for BSE investors
items.description: Jefferies expects Sensex weekly options on BSE to match Nifty’s scale by FY29, driven by strong derivatives growth. However, it warns that much optimism is already priced in, citing valuation concerns, regulatory risks and heavy reliance on a single product. The brokerage maintains a cautious ‘Hold’ stance on BSE.

items.title: Britannia shares fall 5% despite decent Q4 show. Do Morgan Stanley, Nomura see any upside?
items.description: Britannia Industries shares dropped significantly even as the company reported a profit increase.  The FMCG major's fourth-quarter earnings missed analyst expectations for revenue and volume growth.  Supply disruptions in international business due to the West Asia conflict impacted March sales.  Despite this, the company sees traction in e-commerce and premium products.  Analysts maintain mixed views on the stock's future performance.

items.title: BHEL shares' 85% returns, strong earnings fuel ownership churn as retail trims while FIIs, MFs raise exposure
items.description: BHEL shares have delivered an impressive 85% return over the past year, fueled by robust earnings. This performance has attracted significant institutional investment, with Foreign Institutional Investors and Mutual Funds substantially increasing their stakes. Retail investors have reduced their holdings.

items.title: LIC’s $2 billion contrarian bet: 10 stocks the DII giant bought while the market bled
items.description: Life Insurance Corporation of India invested nearly $2 billion in 10 stocks during the March quarter's market fall. LIC bought shares in companies like Bajaj Finance, Bharti Airtel, TCS, and Infosys even as their prices dropped. This strategic move saw LIC increase its stake in several companies. The insurer also reduced holdings in other stocks, showing a selective approach.

items.title: BSE shares fall 3% despite Q4 profit surge. Should you buy, sell or hold India’s oldest stock exchange?
items.description: BSE shares dipped despite reporting a 61% surge in March quarter net profit to Rs 797 crore, driven by an 85% revenue increase to Rs 1,564 crore. Transaction charges were the primary growth driver, soaring 114% year-on-year. Nuvama maintains a 'Buy' rating, citing BSE's lower impact from weekly contract reductions and significant headroom for derivatives customer growth.

items.title: Sensex drops 400 points, Nifty near 24,200; broader markets slip into the red
items.description: Indian stock markets experienced a second day of decline, with both the Sensex and Nifty 50 shedding over half a percent. The Sensex fell approximately 400 points to 77,448, and the Nifty 50 dropped 113 points to 24,214. Despite this dip, midcap and smallcap indices showed resilience, outperforming the broader benchmarks. Market volatility remained stable.

items.title: Sony forecasts 11% rise in annual profit but lower sale
items.description: Sony anticipates a sales dip in its gaming division. This is due to fewer PlayStation 5 hardware sales as the console ages and increased memory chip costs. However, the company projects a profit increase driven by strong first-party game releases. Sony is also investing in its future gaming platform. The company plans a significant share buyback program.

items.title: Kissht parent OnEMI Tech shares soar 11% after strong D-Street debut. Should you buy, sell, or hold?
items.description: OnEMI Technology Solutions shares saw a strong debut, jumping 11% on their listing day. The company operates digital lending platforms Kissht and Ring. Analysts suggest caution due to potential volatility but highlight the company's customer base and technology. Strong financial growth and a large user base position it for future opportunities in India's credit market.

items.title: ​Coinbase Q1 2026: Crypto slowdown weighs on earnings
items.description: Coinbase reported a net loss of $394 million in the first quarter, marking its second consecutive quarterly loss. The company also experienced a decline in revenue as weaker cryptocurrency sentiment led to reduced overall trading activity. Investors reacted negatively to the results, leading to a stock price fall after the earnings announcement. (Source: CNBC, Bloomberg)

items.title: Axis Bank, HDFC Bank, other bank stocks drop up to 2%, Nifty Bank falls 440 points. What lies ahead?
items.description: Banking stocks dragged the Nifty Bank index lower by nearly 440 points amid weakness in heavyweight lenders like HDFC Bank and Axis Bank. Broader market pressure from rising oil prices and FII outflows weighed on sentiment, while analysts flagged key support and resistance levels for the index in the near term.

items.title: Shakti Pumps shares tumble 7% as Q4 profit drops 65% YoY
items.description: Shakti Pumps saw revenue climb significantly. However, costs rose sharply, impacting profits. Earnings per share dropped considerably. Despite this, the board proposed a dividend. The company's stock has fallen over the past year. Institutional investors have reduced their holdings, indicating a cautious market sentiment.

items.title: Jefferies blames HDFC Bank controversy for impacting banking sector valuations
items.description: Jefferies said the leadership uncertainty at HDFC Bank has become a major overhang for the banking sector, dragging benchmark valuations despite strong fundamentals. The brokerage believes clarity on the bank’s management succession, along with easing West Asia tensions, could trigger a recovery in sector earnings and valuations.

items.title: HFCL shares drop 2% after skyrocketing 92% in one month. Time to buy or better to wait?
items.description: HFCL shares saw a 2% dip after a significant 92% surge in a month which prompted profit booking. Despite this, the stock has rallied nearly 147% year-to-date. Analysts at Geojit maintain a 'Buy' rating with a target of Rs 150, citing a strong order book, defense sector expansion, and favorable long-term fiber demand outlook.

items.title: AI trade turns Adani’s energy stocks into India proxy play
items.description: Adani Group's significant investment in green-powered data centers is driving substantial gains in its energy units, positioning them as key AI infrastructure plays in India. The conglomerate's ambitious plans to develop AI-ready data centers, coupled with India's surging electricity demand, have propelled Adani's energy stocks to outperform the market.

items.title: 10 midcap stocks crash up to 50% from their peaks. Are you holding any?
items.description: The stock has declined 50% to Rs 723 from its 52-week high of Rs 1,435.

items.title: Vikram Solar shares slide 5% as Q4 margins take a hit; profit jumps 21% YoY
items.description: Vikram Solar shares fell sharply on Friday as Q4 margins contracted sharply, even though profit rose 21% year-on-year. Revenue grew 22% and EBITDA improved modestly, but a 300-bps margin decline weighed on sentiment. Despite strong FY26 growth, near-term cost pressures from China’s policy changes could affect pricing.

items.title: Smallcaps & midcaps rally! Firstsource Solutions, Nuvama, Godfrey Phillips, other stocks jump up to 16%
items.description: Smallcap and midcap stocks outperformed benchmarks on Friday, with select names rallying up to 16% despite broader market weakness. Gains were driven by earnings momentum and stock-specific triggers, even as geopolitical tensions and high oil prices kept overall sentiment cautious. Analysts continue to track volatility and broader market direction.

items.title: Coforge shares surge 6%, rally 16% in three days post Q4 results. What's ahead for investors?
items.description: Coforge shares saw a significant jump following robust Q4 financial results. The company reported a substantial surge in net profit and revenue. Analysts are optimistic, with several brokerages issuing 'Buy' recommendations. Strong deal wins and an expanding order book fuel confidence for future growth. The acquisition of Encora is also expected to boost revenue.

items.title: SBI shares plunge 7% after Q4 operating profit falls 16% YoY, NIMs contract 21 bps
items.description: State Bank of India shares dropped 7% after the bank reported margin pressure and weaker operating performance in its March quarter earnings. Net interest margins contracted year-on-year and sequentially, while net interest income declined quarter-on-quarter. Operating profit also saw a fall compared to previous periods.

items.title: Midcaps outperform Nifty, smallcap stocks in Q4, deliver 29% earnings growth: Motilal Oswal
items.description: Midcap companies emerged as the strongest performers in the March quarter earnings season, with profit growth outpacing both largecaps and smallcaps, according to MOFSL. Strong contributions from BFSI, technology and utilities supported performance, while analysts cautioned that volatility linked to West Asia tensions and elevated commodity prices may persist.

items.title: 10 midcap stocks crash up to 50% from their peaks. Are you holding any?
items.description: India’s equity markets have remained highly volatile for quite some time. While the benchmark NIFTY50 has corrected nearly 8% from its 52-week high, the NIFTY Midcap 150 continues to hover around record levels.However, beneath the surface, the story is very different. Several midcap stocks within the index have witnessed steep corrections, falling sharply from their respective yearly peaks. We spotlight the top underperformers that have declined between 35% and 50% from their 52-week highs, highlighting the hidden pockets of weakness amid the market’s resilience. (Data source: ACE Equity)

items.title: AI market crash coming soon? Billionaire investor Paul Tudor Jones says the bulls have another two years
items.description: Global markets, led by tech stocks, have reached record highs fueled by AI enthusiasm. Investor Paul Tudor Jones likens AI's current stage to Microsoft's early dominance and the internet's commercialization, predicting another year or two of growth. However, he warns of a significant market downturn akin to the dot-com bubble's aftermath.
